title: malva parviflora subsp. oxyloba
intro: Malva parviflora subsp. oxyloba, commonly known as the little mallow, is a subspecies of the Malva parviflora plant, a perennial herb native to the Mediterranean region. The little mallow has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties, which include relieving digestive issues and providing anti-inflammatory effects, offering potential health benefits such as soothing digestive problems, reducing inflammation, and alleviating respiratory issues. The therapeutic actions of the little mallow are attributed to its bioactive constituents, including flavonoids, phenolic acids, and mucilages, which exhibit antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and demulcent properties. The bioactive constituents of Malva parviflora subsp. oxyloba also include saponins, which may contribute to its potential therapeutic effects.
